practiceQuestions.q: By what other name is the Government of India Act, 1919 commonly known?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Government of India Act, 1919 is also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, named after Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State for India, and Lord Chelmsford, the Viceroy of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who held the position of the Secretary of State for India when the Act of 1919 was enacted?
practiceQuestions.sol: Edwin Montagu was the Secretary of State for India from 1917 to 1922 and formulated the declaration of 1917 leading to the 1919 Act.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India during the introduction of the Government of India Act, 1919?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lord Chelmsford served as the Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921, co-authoring the Montagu-Chelmsford Report which served as the basis for the 1919 Act.

practiceQuestions.q: The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced which major system of governance at the provincial level?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act introduced dyarchy (rule of two) at the provincial level, dividing provincial subjects into transferred and reserved lists.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, the Indian legislature was made bicameral for the first time. What were the two houses called?
opts: Central Legislative Assembly and Council of State
House of Commons and House of Lords
practiceQuestions.sol: The Indian Legislative Council was replaced by a bicameral system consisting of the Upper House (Council of State) and the Lower House (Central Legislative Assembly).

practiceQuestions.q: Which Act first introduced the principle of communal representation for Muslims by establishing separate electorates, which was expanded to other groups in 1919?
practiceQuestions.sol: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by the Morley-Minto Reforms (GOI Act, 1909). The 1919 Act extended it to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans.

practiceQuestions.q: The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for the establishment of which statutory body for the audit of accounts in India?
opts: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act provided for the appointment of an Auditor-General of India to audit the financial accounts of the central and provincial governments.

practiceQuestions.q: When did the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919 officially come into force?
practiceQuestions.sol: Although passed in 1919, the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms and the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919 came into operation in the year 1921.

practiceQuestions.q: Which office was created in London by the Government of India Act, 1919, to take over some of the functions previously performed by the Secretary of State for India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act created the new office of the High Commissioner for India in London and transferred to him some of the functions of the Secretary of State for India.

practiceQuestions.q: The Government of India Act, 1919 required that a statutory commission be appointed after how many years to inquire into the working of the system?
practiceQuestions.sol: Section 84A of the Act mandated the appointment of a statutory commission at the expiration of 10 years to report on the working of the reforms (which resulted in the Simon Commission).

practiceQuestions.q: How were provincial subjects divided under the system of dyarchy introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dyarchy divided provincial subjects into Reserved subjects (administered by the Governor and his executive council without legislative responsibility) and Transferred subjects (administered by the Governor with ministers responsible to the legislative council).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following subjects was classified under the 'Reserved' category of provincial subjects in the 1919 Act?
practiceQuestions.sol: Reserved subjects included critical matters like Finance, Law and Order, Land Revenue, and Irrigation. Education, Public Health, and Local Self-Government were Transferred subjects.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the principal reason behind the failure of dyarchy at the provincial level under the 1919 Act?
opts: Total lack of elected members in the legislative councils
Control over finance and executive power remaining entirely with the Governor and reserved half
Complete absence of any division of subjects
practiceQuestions.sol: Dyarchy failed because ministers in charge of transferred departments had no control over finance (which was a reserved subject), making real developmental work impossible without the Governor's concurrence and funding from the reserved side.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Government of India Act, 1919 attempt to alter the control of the Secretary of State over the Government of India?
opts: It completely abolished the office of the Secretary of State.
It transferred some of his financial burdens to the British Exchequer.
It gave the Viceroy absolute veto power over the Secretary of State.
It made the Secretary of State directly elected by Indians.
practiceQuestions.sol: A major administrative change was that the salary of the Secretary of State for India, which was previously paid out of Indian revenues, was now to be paid out of the British Exchequer.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the franchise extension introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919?
opts: Universal adult suffrage was granted to all citizens above 21.
Franchise was extended based on property, tax, or educational qualifications, covering a small minority of the population.
Only women were given the right to vote across all provinces.
Voting rights were restricted exclusively to British civil servants.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act extended franchise, but it remained severely limited, based on property, tax-paying capacity, or educational criteria. Only about 3% of the population got voting rights.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the Montagu Declaration of August 1917 with respect to the Act of 1919?
opts: It promised immediate and complete independence (Purna Swaraj) to India.
It declared the gradual introduction of responsible government in India as the goal of British policy.
It partitioned British India along communal lines.
It dissolved the Central Legislative Assembly.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Montagu Declaration of August 20, 1917 explicitly stated that the British goal was the increasing association of Indians in every branch of administration and the gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to the progressive realization of responsible government.

practiceQuestions.q: In the bicameral legislature set up by the 1919 Act, what was the tenure of members in the Council of State (Upper House)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the 1919 Act, the tenure of the Council of State (Upper House) was 5 years, while the tenure of the Central Legislative Assembly (Lower House) was 3 years.

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Government of India Act, 1919 impact the Central Executive Council?
opts: It made the Viceroy completely subservient to the Executive Council.
It mandated that out of the executive members (other than the Commander-in-Chief), at least three must be Indian.
It restricted all executive positions solely to British officials.
It abolished the Executive Council altogether.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Act relaxed central control over provinces and expanded the Viceroy's Executive Council, providing that of its members (excluding the Commander-in-Chief), at least three should be Indian.

practiceQuestions.q: Which feature of the Central Legislature under the 1919 Act allowed the Viceroy to pass laws rejected by the legislature?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Viceroy possessed extraordinary powers, including the power to veto any bill, promulgate ordinances, and 'certify' bills that the legislature had rejected, making them law as if they had been passed.

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the inclusion of women in voting and legislative candidacy under the 1919 Act considered notable, despite its limitations?
opts: It granted equal property rights to women across British India.
It was the first time women were granted the right to vote and run for legislative seats, even though subject to provincial discretion and property qualifications.
Women were appointed directly to the Viceroy's Executive Council.
Women led the reserved departments in provincial cabinets.
practiceQuestions.sol: For the first time, the principle of female franchise was recognized, allowing women to vote and stand for election, though provinces had the power to enact this and it was restricted by property qualifications.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It introduced dyarchy in the provinces for the first time.
2. It relaxed central control over the provinces by demarcating and separating the central and provincial subjects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy at the provincial level and notably relaxed central control by demarcating central and provincial subjects while keeping the structure unitary.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the bicameral arrangement introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The lower house was called the Central Legislative Assembly and the upper house was called the Council of State.
2. Both houses had equal powers with respect to the budget and appropriation bills.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct; the legislature became bicameral with the Council of State as the upper house and the Central Legislative Assembly as the lower house. Statement 2 is incorrect because the budget could be voted upon only by the Legislative Assembly, and the Council of State had no power to vote on demands for grants.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the communal representation provisions under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It restricted separate electorates exclusively to Muslims, continuing the policy from the 1909 Act without any extension.
2. It extended the principle of communal representation to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect as separate electorates were expanded. Statement 2 is correct because the 1919 Act extended separate electorates for Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans, deepening the communal divide.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the franchise and voting rights under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. It introduced universal adult franchise for all Indian citizens above the age of 21.
2. The right to vote was restricted and based on property, tax, or educational qualifications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect as universal adult franchise was not introduced until the Constitution of India in 1950. Statement 2 is correct because voting rights were tied to strict property, tax, and educational thresholds.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the creation of the High Commissioner for India under the 1919 Act:
1. The High Commissioner for India was stationed in London to look after trade and agency functions for India.
2. Some of the functions previously performed by the Secretary of State for India were transferred to the High Commissioner.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Act created the office of the High Commissioner for India in London, who took over certain agency functions in the UK previously handled by the Secretary of State.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding provincial subjects under dyarchy in the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. Reserved subjects were administered by the Governor with the aid of ministers responsible to the legislative council.
2. Transferred subjects were administered by the Governor without being responsible to the legislative council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect because they are interchanged. Transferred subjects were administered with ministers responsible to the legislature, whereas Reserved subjects were administered without such responsibility.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Statutory Commission provided under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The Act provided for the appointment of a commission after 10 years to investigate the progress of the governance scheme.
2. This provision led to the appointment of the Simon Commission in 1927, two years ahead of the stipulated 10-year schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Section 84A of the 1919 Act mandated a commission after 10 years, resulting in the Simon Commission being appointed in November 1927 (ahead of 1929).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Legislature under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The members of both the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly were entirely nominated by the Viceroy with no elected element.
2. The Act introduced direct elections to a major extent for both houses of the central legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the majority of members in both houses were elected. Statement 2 is correct as the Act introduced direct elections for both the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the limitations of the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. Executive authority at the center remained completely unaccountable to the central legislature.
2. The Viceroy retained overriding powers to veto legislation and enact ordinances against the wishes of the legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Although the legislature was expanded and made bicameral, the executive was not responsible to it, and the Viceroy held absolute overriding and veto powers.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the provisions for women under the Government of India Act, 1919:
1. The Act mandated that at least 50% of seats in the provincial legislative councils be reserved for women.
2. The Act granted women the right to vote, making India one of the first countries in the British Empire to extend franchise to women on a limited basis.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is completely incorrect; there was no 50% reservation for women. Statement 2 is correct as the 1919 Act recognized female franchise, opening voting rights to women for the first time subject to property qualifications.
